test.title: Section 2 · annual leave and warehouse safety

texts.label: A
texts.title: Annual leave: what staff need to know

paragraphs.text: Annual leave: what staff need to know. The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Full-time staff receive twenty-eight days including public holidays, rising to thirty-three days after five years of service; part-time staff receive the same entitlement in proportion to the hours they work. Leave is requested through the rota system at least two weeks before the first day off, and requests of more than five consecutive days should be made a month ahead so that cover can be arranged.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Managers approve requests in the order they arrive, not in order of seniority. Where two people in the same team ask for the same week and only one can be released, the request made first is granted; if both arrived on the same day, the manager will speak to both and, failing agreement, will draw lots. A refusal must be explained in writing within five working days, and staff who believe a refusal was unfair may raise it with the department head.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Up to five days may be carried into the next leave year and must be taken before 30 June, after which they are lost. Carrying over more than five days requires written approval from a director and is granted only where leave could not be taken for operational reasons. Staff who leave the company are paid for untaken leave; staff who have taken more leave than they have earned will have the difference deducted from their final salary.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Sickness during booked leave may be converted back into sick leave if a doctor’s note covering those dates is provided within seven days of returning. Unpaid leave of up to four weeks may be requested once in any leave year and is at the manager’s discretion; it does not affect service length for the purpose of the five-year increase. Finally, the company closes between Christmas and the New Year, and three days of the annual entitlement are reserved for that period for all staff.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Warehouse safety: the induction you must complete before your first shift. Every new worker, including agency staff and drivers who load their own vehicles, attends a two-hour session with the shift supervisor. The session covers the traffic plan, the alarm signals, the location of the first-aid points and the rules for working at height. You will not be issued with a gate pass until the session has been recorded against your name in the training log.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The warehouse floor is divided by painted lines. Yellow marks the walkway, which is the only route pedestrians may use; blue marks areas where forklifts and pedestrians share space and where pedestrians have priority; red marks loading bays, which no one may enter on foot while a vehicle is manoeuvring. High-visibility clothing is worn everywhere beyond the office door, and headphones are not permitted anywhere on the floor, since the reversing alarm is the main warning that a machine is moving.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Lifting is limited by weight and by shape. Anything above twenty-five kilograms is moved with equipment rather than by hand, and any load that blocks your view is moved with equipment whatever it weighs. Pallets are stacked no more than three high in the racking and two high on the floor. If a load looks unstable, stop and tell the supervisor; staff are never disciplined for stopping work over a safety concern, and the shift record notes the stoppage rather than the person.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Accidents and near misses are reported on the same form, and the form is completed before the end of the shift in which the event happened. A near miss is anything that could have caused injury but did not, and reporting one is not optional: most of the changes made to the traffic plan in the past two years came from near-miss reports rather than from accidents. The first-aid room is by the canteen, and the names of the trained first-aiders are on the noticeboard at every entrance.
paragraphs.label: D
